what: Several color panels stack on top in turn. Each panel is 140vh, taller than the screen, and sticks below the header band (146px). Its content box inside sticks at the same spot, so the next panel rises from below and fully covers the previous one. It uses only position: sticky with no script, so the scroll feel stays native window scroll · Brand leaves a 450px gap between the screen-height plates (100vh), so the previous plate stays pinned for half a screen before the next one covers it (--fx-h: 100vh · --fx-gap: 450px)

options.--fx-top: Height where the panel sticks (via style), default 0 — a brand header band is 146px
options.--fx-h: Scroll length one panel takes, default 140vh
options.--fx-bp: Below this width items are not stacked but laid out one after another — this can’t be changed with CSS variables, so in the consumer’s media query [data-fx-part=panel] position set to relative (Brand 820px)
options.[data-fx-part=panel]: Stacked panels (children, multiple) — background color goes on the panel
options.[data-fx-part=inner]: Optional content slot inside the panel — sticks in place at screen height (100svh − stick height)
options.--fx-gap: Gap under the panel (via style), default 0 — the scroll distance a stuck panel stays before it is covered. Original features panel 450px

from.where: index.html four colored service About panels (original TopAboutSection-contentSection: 140vh · sticky top 9.125rem, inner cell sticky · height 100svh − 9.125rem)
index.html .bs-features four feature panels (original .top_feature_box: sticky top 0 · screen height · margin-bottom 450px, not stacked below 768px)
